bank.title: Biology · High-school practice
bank.description: Twelve questions on cells, genetics, and ecosystems. Practise the basics, explain ideas in your own words, or try a short exam.
bank.author: quitsar

images.alt: A cutaway illustration of an animal cell. A points to a large purple structure containing a darker round body, B to the outer boundary, and C to the pale blue material between the structures. Smaller orange structures have folded inner membranes.

options.rationale: A points to the large purple nucleus. It contains most of the cell’s DNA.
Mitochondria are the smaller orange structures with folded inner membranes.
Ribosomes are the small dots in the cytoplasm and on the rough endoplasmic reticulum.

questions.explanation: A is the nucleus, B marks the cell membrane, and C marks the cytoplasm. The nucleus contains most of the cell’s DNA and helps control cell activities.

questions.prompt: What is the role of the nucleus in an animal cell?

acceptedAnswer.display: The nucleus contains the cell’s DNA and helps control the cell’s activities.
aliases: It stores genetic information and controls cell activities.
acceptedAnswer.feedback: Mention DNA and the control of cell activities.

questions.explanation: The nucleus holds most of an animal cell’s DNA. Its genes provide instructions for making proteins, which help control what the cell does.

questions.prompt: Which organelle releases most of the energy from glucose during aerobic respiration?

options.rationale: Most stages of aerobic respiration take place in mitochondria, producing ATP that the cell can use.
The nucleus stores DNA. It is not where most ATP is made during aerobic respiration.
Ribosomes make proteins rather than carrying out aerobic respiration.

questions.explanation: Mitochondria use the products of glucose breakdown and oxygen to make most of the ATP produced during aerobic respiration.

questions.prompt: Which structures are found in photosynthetic plant cells but not in animal cells?

options.rationale: Plant cells have a cellulose cell wall outside the cell membrane.
Chloroplasts carry out photosynthesis in photosynthetic plant cells. Animal cells do not have them.
Both plant and animal cells usually have a nucleus.
Both plant and animal cells have a cell membrane.

questions.explanation: Plant cells have a cellulose cell wall. Photosynthetic plant cells also have chloroplasts. Both plant and animal cells have a cell membrane and usually a nucleus.

questions.prompt: Why can a high temperature stop an enzyme from working?

acceptedAnswer.display: High temperatures can change the shape of an enzyme’s active site, so the substrate no longer fits. This is called denaturation.
aliases: The enzyme denatures and its active site changes shape.

questions.explanation: Enzymes are proteins. Excessive heat can disrupt the bonds that maintain their shape, changing the active site and reducing or stopping their activity.

questions.prompt: Which substances do plants use to make glucose during photosynthesis?

options.rationale: Photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide and water, with energy from light, to make glucose.
Glucose and oxygen are products of photosynthesis, not its starting substances.
Neither nitrogen gas nor oxygen is a starting substance in the photosynthesis equation.

questions.explanation: In photosynthesis, light energy is used to turn carbon dioxide and water into glucose. Oxygen is released as a by-product.

questions.prompt: Which statements about DNA copying and mitosis are correct?

options.text: DNA is copied before mitosis begins.
options.rationale: DNA replication happens during interphase, before mitosis.

options.text: The daughter cells usually have the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell.
options.rationale: Mitosis separates copied chromosomes into two nuclei, preserving chromosome number.

options.text: Mitosis halves the chromosome number to make gametes.
options.rationale: Meiosis, rather than mitosis, halves the chromosome number when gametes form.

options.text: Mitosis normally produces daughter cells with different sets of genes.
options.rationale: In the absence of mutations, mitosis produces genetically identical daughter cells.

questions.explanation: DNA is copied before mitosis. The copied chromosomes are then separated so that each daughter cell receives a complete set.

questions.prompt: Which two structures are labelled A and B?

images.alt: A cutaway illustration of an animal cell. A points to a large purple structure containing a darker round body, B to the outer boundary, and C to the pale blue material between the structures. Smaller orange structures have folded inner membranes.

options.rationale: A points to the nucleus near the center of the cell.
B points to the thin boundary surrounding the cell.
This is an animal cell. It has no chloroplasts.
Animal cells have a cell membrane but no cell wall.

questions.explanation: A is the nucleus and B is the cell membrane. C marks the cytoplasm. These structures are found in typical animal cells.

questions.prompt: Which organism is the primary consumer in this food chain?

images.alt: A food chain with arrows from grass to grasshopper, from grasshopper to frog, and from frog to snake. Arrows show the direction of energy transfer.

options.rationale: The grasshopper eats the producer, grass, so it is the primary consumer.
The frog eats the grasshopper, making it the secondary consumer in this chain.
Grass makes its own food by photosynthesis, so it is the producer.

questions.explanation: A primary consumer feeds on a producer. Here, energy passes from grass to the grasshopper, then to the frog and snake.

questions.prompt: How can a long-term shortage of food affect a rabbit population?

acceptedAnswer.display: The population may decrease because fewer rabbits survive and reproduce.
aliases: Fewer rabbits may survive or have offspring.
acceptedAnswer.feedback: Explain how food availability affects survival or reproduction.

questions.explanation: Food is a limiting factor. A sustained shortage can increase deaths, reduce reproduction, or cause rabbits to move elsewhere, reducing the local population.

questions.prompt: Two parents each have the alleles Bb. What is the chance that their child inherits bb?

options.rationale: Each parent has a 1 in 2 chance of passing on b. Multiplying 1/2 by 1/2 gives 1/4.
50% is the chance that one parent passes on b, not that both do.
75% is the chance of inheriting at least one B allele in this cross.

questions.explanation: The four equally likely combinations are BB, Bb, bB, and bb. One out of four is bb, so the chance is 25%.

questions.prompt: Which processes return carbon dioxide to the atmosphere?

options.rationale: Respiration releases carbon dioxide as organisms break down carbon-containing molecules.
Combustion releases stored carbon as carbon dioxide.
Photosynthesis takes carbon dioxide out of the atmosphere to build sugars.
Carbon stored in growing wood is held in biomass rather than released to the atmosphere.

questions.explanation: Respiration and combustion release carbon dioxide. Photosynthesis removes it, and some of that carbon can remain stored in plant biomass.
